# Grafana Secrets Manager Provider

<!-- status autogenerated section -->
<!-- end autogenerated section -->

## Summary

This package provides a `confmap.Provider` implementation (`grafanasecretsmanager`) that lets the
Collector reference secrets in its configuration using the placeholder
`${grafanasecretsmanager:<secret_name>}`.

The Collector **never** contacts Grafana Fleet Management directly. Instead, this provider reads
secret values from a loopback endpoint exposed by the OpAMP supervisor, which brokers the secrets
from Grafana Fleet Management over its already-authenticated, TLS-secured OpAMP connection. The
supervisor keeps the secrets in memory and serves them to the collector on `127.0.0.1` only.

## How it works

- Use the placeholder `${grafanasecretsmanager:<secret_name>}` anywhere in the collector
  configuration.
- You can provide a default value with the `:-` suffix:
  `${grafanasecretsmanager:<secret_name>:-<default>}`. The default is used when the secret name is
  empty or the secret is not found.
- The provider is configured through environment variables (a `confmap.Provider` cannot read the
  collector configuration for its own settings). The OpAMP supervisor injects these into the
  collector process:
  - `GRAFANA_SECRETS_MANAGER_ENDPOINT` — the loopback URL of the supervisor's secrets endpoint, e.g.
    `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`.
  - `GRAFANA_SECRETS_MANAGER_TOKEN` — a per-run bearer token authenticating the collector to that
    loopback endpoint.

The provider issues `GET {GRAFANA_SECRETS_MANAGER_ENDPOINT}/{secret_name}` with an
`Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_SECRETS_MANAGER_TOKEN}` header and expects a JSON body of the form
`{"value": "<secret_value>"}`. A `404` response means the secret was not found.

## Security notes

- The loopback port is reachable by other processes on the same host, so access is gated by the
  per-run bearer token (regenerated each run and known only to the supervisor and the collector it
  launched). A loopback transport is used for portability across all supported operating systems.
- Secret values are held only in memory and are never written to disk by the provider.
- The provider never logs secret values or the bearer token.
- To keep secrets out of logs and effective-config dumps, reference them from configuration fields
  typed as `configopaque.String` (most receiver/exporter/extension password, token, and API-key
  fields already are).

## Example

```yaml
exporters:
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: https://example.com
    headers:
      authorization: ${grafanasecretsmanager:otlp-token}
```
